newsitem.title: USA: Sept S&P 500 futures turn down after opening pop.
newsitem.headline: Sept S&P 500 futures turn down after opening pop.

text.p: September S&P 500 stock index futures erased opening gains and turned lower after a U.S. investment house emerged as an aggressive seller in early pit trade, pushing prices into sell stops, floor traders said.
"There was no news behind the downturn," one brokerage trader said.
A second large house joined in the selling, and losses escalated in the relatively lightly traded market, traders said.
"Everyone kind of jumped on the bandwagon," said the brokerage trader.
Traders said the focus remained on this week's corporate earnings releases, with key results including Intel and Microsoft still eagerly awaited.
This morning, several higher than forecast earnings reports buoyed stock index futures before the downturn, traders said.
September bond futures' recovery following the release of U.S. June retail sales data also helped underpin stock futures, the traders said. Retail sales rose 0.5 percent.
Another broker in S&P futures said retail sales were expected to rebound after recent weather-related weakness.
Local traders were generally fearful of getting short the market amid sentiment that another contract high is in the cards, he said.
This morning, September S&Ps traded up to a high of 929.50, just below Monday's daily high, and continue to hover within striking distance of the contract high of 932.25 set July 7.
Sell-stops were triggered around 923.50 and 922.50 on the pullback, helping push the September contract to the session low so far of 920.80, traders said.

S&P 500 futures were down 2.95 points at 923.90, Nasdaq 100s rose 6.75 to 1061.00, Russell 2000s were up 0.35 points at 408.80, Nikkei 225 index futures fell 160.0 to 20,165.0 and Midcap 400s rose 1.20 points to 304.70.
